references.mutcd_2009_4e06: FHWA, Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 2009 edition with revisions 1 and 2, Section 4E.06: paragraph 7 (pedestrian clearance time at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second), paragraph 11 (walk interval at least 7 seconds), paragraph 12 (walk intervals as short as 4 seconds may be used) and paragraph 14 (walk plus clearance at 3 feet per second from a point 6 feet from the curb)
references.mutcd_2023_4f17: FHWA, Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 11th edition (2023), Section 4F.17 paragraph 13: a yellow change interval of 3 to 6 seconds and a red clearance interval not exceeding 6 seconds

entries.label: Fixed-time two-phase plan, 60 second cycle, with concurrent pedestrian walks

sources.intervals[0].duration_ms: cited mutcd_2009_4e06: paragraph 11, a walk interval of at least 7 seconds
sources.intervals[1].duration_ms: declared: the rest of a 30 second phase in a fixed-time plan for the synthetic network, not an optimised timing; the compiler checks that it covers pedestrian clearance at 3.5 feet per second for every crossing the group governs
sources.intervals[2].duration_ms: cited mutcd_2023_4f17: a yellow change interval of 3 to 6 seconds; 4 seconds is chosen inside that range
sources.intervals[3].duration_ms: cited mutcd_2023_4f17: a red clearance interval of at most 6 seconds; 2 seconds is chosen inside that range
sources.intervals[4].duration_ms: cited mutcd_2009_4e06: paragraph 11, a walk interval of at least 7 seconds
sources.intervals[5].duration_ms: declared: the rest of a 30 second phase in a fixed-time plan for the synthetic network, not an optimised timing; the compiler checks that it covers pedestrian clearance at 3.5 feet per second for every crossing the group governs
sources.intervals[6].duration_ms: cited mutcd_2023_4f17: a yellow change interval of 3 to 6 seconds; 4 seconds is chosen inside that range
sources.intervals[7].duration_ms: cited mutcd_2023_4f17: a red clearance interval of at most 6 seconds; 2 seconds is chosen inside that range
